papers.title: Designing versatile sandwich-like magnetic Nb2O5 nanocomposites derived from Nb2C MXene for phosphopeptide enrichment.
papers.authors: Zhang S, Lu Y, Qiao JQ, Lian HZ
papers.abstract:
The enrichment of phosphopeptides prior to their detection is essential for the identification of protein phosphorylation followed by matrix assisted laser desorption/ionization time-of-flight mass spectrometry because of their low concentration, low deionization efficiency and suppression from the interference derived from high-abundance counterparts. Niobium-based affinity materials have great potential in the enrichment of phosphopeptide enrichment, yet have not been extensively studied. To date, there are no reports on the application of Nb2CTx-based materials in separation science, especially in the application in phosphopeptide enrichment.
In this work, Nb2C MXene derived sandwich-like magnetic Nb2O5 nanocomposites (denoted as m-Nb2O5-Fe2O3) were designed and synthesized for the first time by HF-etching of Nb2AlC MAX phase, in situ growth of Fe3O4 nanoparticles and calcination in air. The nanocomposites were then applied as magnetic solid-phase extraction (MSPE) adsorbents in the enrichment of phosphopeptides through the synergistic metal oxide affinity chromatography mechanism by Nb-O and Fe-O. The MSPE method exhibited extremely low detection limit (0.1 nmol L-1 of β-casein), great anti-interference ability (1:2000 of the molar ratio of β-casein to bovine serum albumin), good reusability (3 cycles) and satisfactory recovery (87.6%). The universality of m-Nb2O5-Fe2O3 was further verified by the successful application in non-fat milk, human saliva and a traditional Chinese medicine injection.
The m-Nb2O5-Fe2O3 nanocomposites are able to enrich phosphopeptides with high efficiency from diverse samples, thanks to the layered structure which provides abundant specific binding sites of Nb-O and Fe-O towards phosphate groups in phosphopeptides. The composites show great potential as a promising material for phosphopeptide enrichment from complex biological and biomedical samples.

papers.title: Yupingfeng alleviates allergic rhinitis by modulating gut microbiota and succinate to inhibit mTOR/S6K signaling.
papers.authors: Zuo Y, Li Y, Huang Z, Zeng H, Liu Q, Zhou Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Yupingfeng granules (YPF), derived from the classic traditional Chinese medicine prescription Yupingfeng powder, have been recommended in clinical practice guidelines for the management of allergic rhinitis (AR), and their clinical efficacy is widely recognized. However, the underlying pharmacological mechanisms have not been thoroughly investigated.
This study aimed to investigate whether YPF protects the nasal epithelial barrier and alleviates AR by modulating the gut microbiota and pathways related to its metabolites.
An OVA-induced AR mouse model was established and phenotypically evaluated. The dependence of YPF efficacy on gut microbiota was assessed by 16S rRNA sequencing, antibiotic depletion, and fecal microbiota transplantation. 1H-NMR metabolomics was used to identify key metabolites, followed by exogenous supplementation for validation. Nasal mucosal transcriptome sequencing was performed to explore downstream pathways, and functional validation was conducted in OVA-induced HNEpCs through metabolite intervention, YPF co-treatment, mTOR knockdown, and MHY1485 treatment.
YPF dose-dependently reduced nasal rubbing and sneezing, attenuated IgE-mediated type 2 inflammation, and ameliorated nasal epithelial barrier injury in OVA-induced AR mice. YPF remodeled the gut microbiota and increased microbial diversity. Gut microbiota depletion attenuated the protective effects of YPF, whereas FMT from YPF donors reproduced them. Metabolomic analysis identified succinate as a key YPF-responsive metabolite, and exogenous succinate aggravated nasal epithelial barrier injury. Transcriptomic analysis suggested that succinate-induced nasal mucosal injury may involve mTOR signaling activation. In vitro, succinate aggravated OVA-induced barrier injury in HNEpCs, with disrupted Occludin distribution and enhanced mTOR/S6K phosphorylation, whereas YPF co-treatment reversed these changes. mTOR knockdown mimicked the protective effects of YPF, whereas MHY1485 attenuated them.
YPF alleviates OVA-induced AR by remodeling the gut microbiota, reducing succinate accumulation, and suppressing mTOR/S6K signaling to preserve nasal epithelial barrier integrity.

papers.title: Mechanisms underlying the promotion of intestinal absorption of baohuoside I by Dipsacus asperoides saponin fractions and their synergistic anti‑osteoporosis efficacy in combination.
papers.authors: Li M, Guo N, Zhong Q, Qi Z, Xia M, Feng L et al.
papers.abstract: Baohuoside I (BA) is the key active ingredient in the compound anti-osteoporosis preparation Xianlinggubao; however, its poor solubility and permeability result in low oral bioavailability. This study systematically investigated, from both pharmaceutical and pharmacological perspectives, the role of Dipsacus asperoides saponins fractions (DAS) in enhancing BA absorption and their synergistic anti-osteoporosis effects. From a pharmaceutical perspective, DAS significantly improves BA's solubility, membrane permeability, and gastrointestinal stability, and forms nanocomposites with BA through noncovalent interactions (as verified by DSC, TEM, FT-IR, and molecular dynamics simulations). In vivo intestinal perfusion experiments in rats confirmed that DAS enhances BA absorption in all intestinal segments; in a Caco-2 monolayer cell model, DAS inhibited MRP2/BCRP efflux and reversibly opened tight junctions, increasing the apparent permeability coefficient of BA from (1.62 ± 0.21) × 10⁻⁶ to (4.25 ± 0.45) × 10⁻⁶ cm/s; Oral pharmacokinetic studies in rats further confirmed that the AUC0-∞ was significantly higher in the BA-DAS combination group. Pharmacologically, in an ovariectomized mouse model, the combination of BA and DAS significantly improved bone microstructure and serum bone metabolism markers compared to BA alone. Urinary non-targeted metabolomics results further revealed that this synergistic effect is associated with the regulation of Ascorbate and aldarate metabolism, Glycine, serine, and threonine metabolism, and Tryptophan metabolism pathways. In summary, DAS promotes BA absorption through a dual mechanism of inhibiting efflux and opening tight junctions, and the combination of BA and DAS produces a synergistic anti-osteoporotic effect, providing a mechanistic explanation for the formulation of traditional Chinese medicine.

papers.title: Electroacupuncture analgesia for cancer-related pain.
papers.journal: Current opinion in supportive and palliative care
papers.authors: Fuller AM, Sikandar S
papers.abstract:
Cancer-related pain remains a major clinical problem arising from both malignancy and its treatment. Current pharmacotherapies rely on opioids and adjuvant analgesics, which still provide unsatisfactory relief for the majority of patients. The use of complementary therapies for the management of cancer-related pain is growing, and acupuncture is increasingly incorporated into integrative cancer care. We explore the clinical and preclinical evidence base for the use of electroacupuncture in tumour-associated pain and treatment-associated pain, with an emphasis on experimental studies of cancer-induced bone pain and chemotherapy-induced pain.
Preclinical studies provide increasing biological plausibility for electroacupuncture analgesia by regulating peripheral and central neuroimmune and neuromodulatory nociceptive axes. Still, greater mechanistic alignment between preclinical and clinical studies is needed to understand how the mechanisms of acupuncture in rodents translate to humans. Clinical literature supports an analgesic effect of acupuncture; however, the magnitude and consistency of benefit vary considerably between studies. The biological activity of sham acupuncture further complicates the interpretation of conventional placebo-controlled trials and highlights the importance of incorporating objective physiological outcomes alongside patient-reported measures.
Improved standardisation and reporting, objective outcome measures, and adequately powered trials that distinguish cancer-related pain phenotypes and acupuncture modalities will be necessary to establish how acupuncture can be optimally integrated into evidence-based cancer-related pain care.

papers.title: Clinical Outcomes of High-Flow Nasal Cannula Combined with Standardized Acupoint Application in Acute Exacerbations of COPD: A Retrospective Study.
papers.journal: International journal of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease
papers.authors: Li B, Lu Y, Pan L, Xu X, Zhu W, Zhang D et al.
papers.abstract:
To evaluate the clinical outcomes associated with adding standardized acupoint application (AA) to high-flow nasal cannula (HFNC) in hospitalized patients with acute exacerbation of COPD (AECOPD).
This retrospective comparative effectiveness study included 178 consecutive AECOPD patients treated between February 2024 and April 2025 who received either HFNC alone (n=89) or HFNC plus AA (n=89). All patients received guideline-based conventional care. Propensity score matching was used to adjust for baseline differences. Clinical outcomes were assessed at day 10, including a validated Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) syndrome-scoring scale (primary outcome), selected to holistically capture the multi-symptom response targeted by the integrative intervention, pulmonary function (FEV1, FVC), arterial blood gases (PaO2, PaCO2, SaO2), inflammatory biomarkers (IL-8, IL-17, TNF-α, hs-CRP, PCT), immune subsets (CD4⁺, CD8⁺, CD4⁺/CD8⁺ ratio), and patient-centered outcomes (CAT, mMRC, 6MWD, SGRQ).
The HFNC plus AA group showed a higher clinical response rate (88.76% vs 70.79%; adjusted risk difference, 17.98%; relative risk, 1.25; 95% CI, 1.08-1.46; P=0.003). The combination group demonstrated greater improvements in FEV1 (mean difference [MD] 0.07 L), FVC (MD 0.20 L), PaO2 (MD 5.03 mmHg), and PaCO2 (MD -1.93 mmHg) (all P<0.05). Reductions in inflammatory markers (IL-8, IL-17, TNF-α, hs-CRP, PCT) and favorable immune modulation (increased CD4⁺/CD8⁺ ratio) were more pronounced in the HFNC plus AA group (all P<0.01). Patient-centered outcomes also favored the combination: CAT (MD -2.59), 6MWD (MD 28.53 m), and SGRQ (MD -5.76) (all P≤0.01). Adverse events were higher in the combination group (47.67% vs 32.18%; RR 1.48; 95% CI 1.02-2.16), driven primarily by local skin reactions.
In this observational study, adding standardized AA to HFNC was associated with improved clinical outcomes and a generally manageable safety profile. However, these findings are exploratory and require prospective validation.

papers.title: Effectiveness, Safety, and Cost-Effectiveness of Ultrasound-Guided Acupotomy for Degenerative Cervical Radiculopathy: A Protocol for a Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.authors: Cho S, An S, Jung H, Kim M, Kim J, Kang BK et al.
papers.abstract:
Degenerative cervical radiculopathy (CR) causes neck and upper-extremity pain, sensory disturbance, and motor dysfunction resulting from nerve root compression or irritation by disc herniation, foraminal narrowing, or spondylotic changes. Ultrasound-guided acupotomy (UA), a minimally invasive acupuncture-based intervention, permits real-time visualization of target tissues and adjacent neurovascular structures, enabling controlled release of fibrotic or adhesive soft tissues that may contribute to nerve root compression. Evidence on its effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness remains limited.
This two-arm, parallel, single-center randomized controlled trial will enroll 56 patients with clinically and radiologically confirmed degenerative CR, randomized 1:1 to UA or conventional physical therapy (CPT; interferential current therapy and microwave diathermy). Both groups will receive six sessions over 3 weeks, with follow-up at weeks 4, 7, and 11. The primary outcome is the between-group difference in mean change from baseline in visual analog scale scores for cervical and/or upper-extremity pain/discomfort at week 4. Secondary outcomes include painDETECT, Neck Disability Index, EuroQol 5-dimension 5-level, Depression Anxiety Stress Scales-21, Patient Global Impression of Change, clinically important difference, rescue medication use, Work Productivity and Activity Impairment, and cervical multifidus stiffness on shear wave elastography (SWE), interpreted as exploratory. Adverse events will be recorded at every visit.
This trial will evaluate the effectiveness, safety, and cost-effectiveness of UA versus CPT for degenerative CR. By integrating clinical outcomes, economic evaluation, magnetic resonance imaging-based foraminal stenosis grading, and exploratory SWE assessment, findings may provide comprehensive evidence on the role of UA in CR management.
This protocol was approved by the Institutional Review Board of Pusan National University Korean Medicine Hospital. Written informed consent will be obtained from each participant after the study aims, procedures, and potential risks have been explained.
Clinical Research Information Service, KCT0011139; registered on 12 November 2025.

papers.title: Comparative Efficacy of Acupuncture-Based Interventions for Cervicogenic Headache: A Systematic Review and Network Meta-Analysis.
papers.authors: Xia L, Lu Y, Guo K, Yang D
papers.abstract:
To compare the relative efficacy of acupuncture-based interventions for cervicogenic headache and identify approaches that may improve overall efficacy rate and pain intensity.
PubMed, Embase, the Cochrane Library, Web of Science, and CNKI were searched from inception through September 26, 2026 for randomized controlled trials. Two reviewers independently screened studies, extracted data, and assessed risk of bias using the Cochrane Risk of Bias 2 tool. A frequentist random-effects network meta-analysis synthesized direct and indirect evidence. Outcomes were the study-defined overall efficacy rate and pain intensity measured with the Visual Analog Scale (VAS). Treatment rankings, sensitivity analyses, small-study effects, and confidence in network estimates using the Confidence in Network Meta-Analysis (CINeMA) framework were evaluated.
Twenty-nine randomized trials were included. All 29 contributed to the overall efficacy rate network, and 16 trials (1300 participants) contributed to the VAS network. Compared with conventional acupuncture, needle-knife therapy, Fu's subcutaneous needling (FSN), fire needling, warm acupuncture, and special manual acupuncture significantly improved the overall efficacy rate. Needle-knife therapy ranked highest, followed by FSN and fire needling. For pain intensity, fire needling produced the largest reduction versus conventional acupuncture (MD, -1.88; 95% CI, -2.70 to -1.05), followed by FSN, special manual acupuncture, and warm acupuncture. Needle-knife therapy did not significantly reduce VAS scores compared with conventional acupuncture. Sensitivity analyses generally supported the findings, although several estimates were influenced by individual studies. According to CINeMA, confidence in the network estimates ranged from moderate to very low for both outcomes, and no comparison achieved high confidence.
Fire needling and FSN showed the most consistently favorable estimates across the two outcomes. Needle-knife therapy may improve the overall efficacy rate, but its advantage for pain relief remains uncertain. Because none of the evaluated comparisons achieved high confidence according to CINeMA, larger multicenter randomized trials with standardized outcomes and longer follow-up are needed.

papers.title: Efficacy of acupuncture for sleep disorders in amnestic mild cognitive impairment: a randomized controlled trial with fMRI.
papers.authors: Qiu D, Li R, Yang J, Ding L, Deng J, Liu Y et al.
papers.abstract:
To access the efficacy of acupuncture in improving sleep disorders in patients with amnestic Mild Cognitive Impairment (aMCI) and to investigate its mechanisms.
Thirty aMCI patients with sleep disorders and fifteen healthy controls (HC) were enrolled. Patients were randomly assigned to verum acupuncture group (VA) or sham acupuncture group (SA) for a 12-week treatment. Assessments included the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA), Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI), and resting-state Functional Magnetic Resonance Imaging (fMRI).
At baseline, patients with aMCI exhibited aberrant brain activity in temporal, frontal, parietal, and cerebellar regions compared with HCs. After treatment, the VA group, but not the SA group, showed significant improvements in both MoCA and PSQI scores. Rs-fMRI analyses revealed significant VA-related changes in the amplitude of low-frequency fluctuation (ALFF) in the left calcarine sulcus and regional homogeneity (ReHo) in the cerebellar vermis. Changes in these imaging indicators were significantly correlated with changes in MoCA scores but not with changes in PSQI scores. Moreover, changes in MoCA scores were negatively correlated with changes in PSQI scores in the VA group (r = -0.536, p = 0.039).
Acupuncture could effectively improve sleep and cognitive function in aMCI patients. The treatment-related alterations in brain function may be associated with changes in the dermatome layer and the brain-cerebellar cortex circuitry.

papers.title: Dietary licorice improves carcass yield, hepatocellular protection, gut health, oxidative status, and cecal bacterial balance in broiler chickens.
papers.authors: Egbu CF, Smit CJ
papers.abstract: Over the past decade, phytotherapy such as licorice has attracted research as an alternative to antibiotic growth promoters in broiler production, driven by rising concerns over antimicrobial resistance. However, the consistency of its effects across productive, physiological, and health outcomes remains inconsistent. This meta-analysis quantitatively synthesized published experimental evidence on the effects of dietary licorice on growth performance, carcass yield, blood indices, visceral organs, oxidative status, intestinal morphology, and cecal bacterial balance in broiler chickens. A systematic literature search identified studies published between 2010 and 2025, and effect sizes were computed (Hedges' g; 95% confidence interval). Pooled estimates were derived under the random-effects model using the restricted maximum likelihood estimator, with between-study heterogeneity characterized by I² and the Q-statistic. Univariable mixed-effects meta-regression was conducted to identify study-level moderators of treatment response, and publication bias was assessed using a funnel plot and the Rosenberg fail-safe N criterion. Dietary licorice did not affect feed intake or the feed conversion ratio, but it did increase body weight gain (BWG; SMD = 0.289; P = 0.002), breast, thigh, gizzard, and bursa weights (P < 0.05). Gut integrity also improved with the villus height/crypt depth ratio (SMD = 0.931; P = 0.041), and Lactobacillus spp. counts (SMD = 0.266; P = 0.003) increased, while Escherichia coli populations were suppressed (SMD = -1.737; P < 0.001). Overall, the findings support that licorice enhances body weight gain, with route, duration, sex, and strain moderating efficacy.

papers.title: Panax ginseng suppresses endothelin-1-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy through inhibition of the local angiotensin II-AT1 receptor signaling axis.
papers.authors: Numata T, Tagashira H, Sato-Numata K, Takayama R, Aoyama A, Sakai A et al.
papers.abstract: Panax ginseng (PG) is a traditional herbal medicine widely used for the treatment of cardiovascular disorders in East Asia. Although PG has been reported to attenuate cardiomyocyte hypertrophy, the molecular mechanisms underlying its cardioprotective effects remain incompletely understood. In this study, we investigated whether modulation of the endothelin-1 (ET-1)-angiotensin II (AngII) signaling axis contributes to the anti-hypertrophic action of PG. Neonatal rat ventricular myocytes (NRVMs) were used to evaluate ET-1-induced hypertrophy, and pharmacological experiments using receptor antagonists were performed to examine the signaling pathways involved. Extracellular AngII levels were quantified by ELISA, intracellular Ca2+ accumulation was assessed in AT1AR-overexpressing NRVMs, and whole-cell patch-clamp recordings were performed in HEK293T cells co-expressing AT1AR and TRPC6. PG significantly attenuated ET-1-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy without altering ETAR or ETBR expression. Pharmacological experiments with the ETAR antagonist BQ-123 suggested that the anti-hypertrophic effect of PG could not be explained solely by direct inhibition of ETAR signaling. PG markedly suppressed ET-1-induced extracellular AngII production, and interaction studies with losartan further implicated the AngII-AT1AR pathway in the anti-hypertrophic action of PG. Moreover, PG inhibited AngII-induced intracellular Ca2+ accumulation in AT1AR-overexpressing NRVMs and attenuated AngII-evoked TRPC6-mediated membrane currents without affecting basal channel activity. These findings demonstrate that PG suppresses ET-1-induced cardiomyocyte hypertrophy by inhibiting both ET-1-induced AngII production and downstream AT1AR-dependent signaling, identifying suppression of the AngII-AT1AR signaling axis as a key mechanism underlying its cardioprotective effects.

papers.title: [Nonpharmacological interventions in perioperative pain management].
papers.authors: Zugaj MR, Erlenwein J, Meißner W, Keßler J
papers.abstract: Nonpharmacological interventions can substantially improve the effectiveness of perioperative pain management. Positive, realistic information and goal setting, together with the deliberate use of communication strategies and placebo effects, can positively influence the experience of pain. Maladaptive cognition and an unnecessary focus on pain can intensify pain perception. Physiotherapy, transcutaneous electrical nerve stimulation (TENS) and acupuncture can be used as adjunctive treatment for selected indications. Music, quiet, appropriate lighting, a pleasant environment and personal belongings are easily implemented environmental factors with potential benefits. Nonpharmacological interventions are not a substitute for established postoperative pharmacological analgesia; however, as low-risk, patient-centered components they should form an integral part of multimodal treatment strategies. Clear responsibilities, appropriate training, interprofessional coordination and realistic patient selection are prerequisites for successful implementation. This article provides a practical overview of the targeted use of these techniques and strategies.

papers.title: Modulating the WNK1-SPAK/OSR1-KCC2 Pathway: Acupuncture's Therapeutic Potential in Mitigating Muscle Hypertonia in Ischemic Stroke Rats.
papers.authors: Sun TY, Ma LX, Zhang WX, Lu SB, Xiu JY, Chen MY
papers.abstract: This study investigated the therapeutic effects of acupuncture on post-stroke muscle hypertonia (PSMH) in rats, focusing on the WNK1-SPAK/OSR1-KCC2 pathway to elucidate its underlying mechanisms and support clinical translation. Behavioral, electrophysiological, TTC staining, AChE staining, and transmission electron microscope analyses were used to assess the efficacy of acupuncture. RT-qPCR, Western blot, and immunofluorescence were used to evaluate the expression of the medullary WNK1-SPAK/OSR1-KCC2 pathway. Pharmacological modulation using WNK463 and Gabazine suggested the involvement of WNK kinase activity. Acupuncture reduced neurological deficits and spasticity, enhanced motor recovery, suppressed spinal motor neuron hyperexcitability, and ameliorated neuromuscular dysfunction and muscular structural abnormality. Mechanistically, it downregulated WNK1, SPAK, and OSR1 and increased membrane KCC2 expression in the medulla oblongata. WNK463 partially mimicked acupuncture's effects, while Gabazine partially reversed them. Acupuncture alleviates muscle hypertonia and enhances locomotor recovery in rats with PSMH, potentially by inhibiting the medullary WNK1-SPAK/OSR1 pathway and thereby upregulating KCC2 expression and membrane localization.

papers.title: Low-dose histrelin for ovulation induction in mares: a partially randomized crossover pilot study.
papers.authors: de Barros Fogagnoli L, Jose KCA, Weckl R, Mota CMO, Fernandes MO, Machado RC et al.
papers.abstract: This partially randomized crossover pilot study evaluated reduced doses of histrelin for ovulation induction in mares and compared intramuscular (IM) administration with pharmacopuncture at the Bai-hui and Yan-chi acupoints. Eleven mares were enrolled, of which nine completed all eight protocols and were included in the analyses. The protocols comprised 250 µg histrelin IM (standard dose), 75 µg IM, 25 µg IM, no intervention, saline at Bai-hui, saline at Yan-chi, 25 µg histrelin at Bai-hui, and 25 µg histrelin at Yan-chi. Ovulation was assessed by transrectal ultrasonography at scheduled examinations until detected, with ovulation within 48 h as the primary outcome. Ovulations first detected at 24 h were excluded from the primary analysis. Ovulation within 48 h occurred in 88.9% (8/9) of observations with 250 µg IM, 87.5% (7/8) with 75 µg IM, 87.5% (7/8) with 25 µg IM, 37.5% (3/8) with no intervention, 50.0% (3/6) with saline at Bai-hui, 100% (9/9) with 25 µg histrelin at Bai-hui, 12.5% (1/8) with saline at Yan-chi, and 87.5% (7/8) with 25 µg histrelin at Yan-chi. Exact 95% confidence intervals were wide, reflecting the small sample size. Exploratory pairwise comparisons with the no-intervention protocol were performed without adjustment for multiple comparisons and should be interpreted cautiously. The findings provide preliminary evidence that reduced histrelin doses, including 25 µg, may induce ovulation within 48 h in mares. However, this study did not demonstrate an advantage of pharmacopuncture over IM administration of the same reduced dose. Larger, fully randomized studies are required to confirm the efficacy of reduced-dose histrelin and determine whether administration at specific acupoints provides any additional effect.

papers.title: Risk-Oriented Clinical Management and Observed Safety Outcomes of Acupuncture in Patients at Risk of Metal Allergy: A Single-Center Retrospective Case Series.
papers.journal: Journal of integrative and complementary medicine
papers.authors: Fujita Y, Kikuchi T, Yamaguchi S, Horibe G, Ibata S, Sekiya T et al.
papers.abstract:
Acupuncture is widely used in complementary and integrative medicine. Because acupuncture needles are primarily made of stainless steel, patients at risk of metal allergy require careful management. However, evidence regarding risk-oriented clinical management and observed safety outcomes remains limited. This study aimed to describe risk-oriented clinical management and observed safety outcomes in routine acupuncture practice, including those at risk of metal allergy.
This single-center retrospective case series included consecutive new patients receiving acupuncture over 1 year. Electronic medical records were reviewed for metal allergy risk, clinical management, and adverse events. Patients were classified as at risk of metal allergy based on documented history, self-reported symptoms, or clinical findings. Clinical management was individualized based on risk assessment, clinical judgment, and patient preferences. Safety outcomes included metal contact allergic reactions, systemic metal allergy reactions, and other serious adverse events.
Among 230 patients, 23 (10.0%) were classified as at risk of metal allergy. Clinical management included risk assessment, stepwise and minimally invasive approaches, consideration of alternative materials, and post-treatment monitoring. Among 22 patients, 220 treatment sessions were performed. No cases of metal contact allergic reactions, systemic metal allergy reactions, or other serious adverse events were observed. Likewise, no such adverse events were observed in the overall study population.
This study provides a practice-based description of risk-oriented clinical management and observed safety outcomes in patients receiving acupuncture, including those at risk of metal allergy. The findings illustrate how patients at risk of metal allergy were assessed and managed in routine acupuncture practice, while the absence of observed adverse events should be interpreted cautiously given the limited sample size and observational study design.

papers.title: Tongsai Granules Ameliorate Airway Mucus Hypersecretion in AECOPD by Remodeling LIPA-Driven Ceramide Metabolism.
papers.authors: Cheng M, Li K, Zhang Z, Xin N, Liu X, Du Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Tongsai Granules (TSG) is a traditional Chinese medicine formula traditionally used for the treatment of acute exacerbation of chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (AECOPD) with phlegm-heat obstructing lung syndrome, a condition characterized by cough, excessive sputum production, and dyspnea; however, its underlying therapeutic mechanisms remain unclear.
To investigate the mechanisms by which TSG alleviates airway mucus hypersecretion in AECOPD through regulation of the LIPA/ceramide axis.
A murine AECOPD model and airway epithelial cells were used. Proteomic and lipidomic analyses, molecular docking, surface plasmon resonance (SPR), drug affinity responsive target stability (DARTS), and LIPA overexpression and knockdown assays were performed.
TSG improved pulmonary function, attenuated lung injury and inflammation, and suppressed MUC5AC expression in AECOPD mice. Multi-omics analyses showed that TSG regulated lipid metabolism and reduced triglyceride and ceramide accumulation while downregulating lysosomal acid lipase A (LIPA). Several serum-exposed constituents of TSG inhibited MUC5AC expression. Bergenin (BER) was selected as a representative bioactive constituent for subsequent target-identification and mechanistic studies. Molecular docking, SPR, and DARTS assays demonstrated direct interaction between BER and LIPA. LIPA knockdown suppressed MUC5AC expression, whereas LIPA overexpression attenuated the inhibitory effect of BER. Moreover, exogenous ceramide reversed BER-mediated suppression of MUC5AC.
TSG alleviates airway mucus hypersecretion in AECOPD by targeting the LIPA/ceramide axis. Bergenin directly targets LIPA to regulate lipid metabolism and suppress MUC5AC overexpression.

papers.title: Short-term Efficacy of massage and related treatments for Ankylosing Spondylitis: A Systematic Review and Meta Analysis.
papers.authors: Shengyang Y, Siqi L, Yangming X, Junjie Z, Bowen Z, Qingguang Z et al.
papers.abstract:
Ankylosing spondylitis (AS) is a chronic inflammatory rheumatic disease causing significant pain, stiffness, and functional impairment. Conventional treatments are limited by adverse events and poor efficacy for axial manifestations, leading AS patients to seek complementary therapies such as massage. However, no systematic reviews or meta-analyses have synthesized evidence on massage for AS, leaving its efficacy unconfirmed.
From inception to July 5, 2025, a comprehensive literature search was conducted using eight electronic databases to identify randomized controlled trials of massage and related treatments for AS. Risk of bias was assessed via Cochrane RoB 2, and data was synthesized using Review Manager 5.4. Subgroup analysis was performed according to the different intervention methods. The I2 statistic was used to assess the heterogeneity.
Seventeen RCTs involving 1,687 patients were included. Meta-analysis demonstrated that massage significantly improved disease activity (Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Disease Activity Index [BASDAI]: SMD = -1.09, 95% CI: -1.38 to -0.80, P < 0.001), physical function (Bath Ankylosing Spondylitis Functional Index [BASFI]: SMD = -1.00, 95% CI: -1.33 to -0.67, P < 0.001), spinal pain (Visual Analog Scale [VAS-pain]: MD = -1.43, 95% CI: -1.80 to -1.05, P < 0.001), and inflammatory markers (erythrocyte sedimentation rate [ESR]: MD = -3.58, 95% CI: -4.71 to -2.99, P < 0.001; C-reactive protein [CRP]: SMD = -0.73, 95% CI: -1.03 to -0.43, P < 0.001) compared to control groups. Subgroup analysis suggested that massage alone might be more effective than massage combined with other therapies like acupuncture. Significant heterogeneity was observed, attributable to variations in massage techniques and protocols. Of note, the long-term efficacy of massage was not evaluated in this review, as no included studies provided follow‑up beyond the treatment period.
Massage and related treatments are effective in alleviating disease activity, improving physical function, reducing pain, and lowering inflammation in patients with ankylosing spondylitis. It can be considered as a beneficial non-pharmacological adjunct for AS. However, these findings must be interpreted with caution due to several limitations inherent in the included studies, including methodological flaws, small sample sizes, inconsistent treatment protocols, and insufficient statistical precision. Moreover, blinding was not feasible in massage therapy, which precludes exclusion of potential placebo or observer effects. Therefore, future high‑quality, standardized, and longitudinal RCTs are warranted to confirm the role of massage in evidence‑based AS management.

papers.title: Therapeutic effects of Stemona japonica extract against Mycoplasma gallisepticum infection: Association with suppression of NF-κB-mediated inflammatory response.
papers.authors: Yao W, Liang X, Zhang Z, Li X, Ma X, Zhao Z et al.
papers.abstract: Mycoplasma gallisepticum (MG) is the primary causative agent of chronic respiratory disease (CRD) in chickens, causing massive economic losses to the global poultry industry. The widespread emergence of antibiotic-resistant MG strains has created an urgent need for safe and effective alternative therapies. Stemona japonica (Baibu), a traditional Chinese medicine with well-documented antitussive and anti-inflammatory properties, has not been systematically evaluated for its anti-MG activity. This study investigated the therapeutic effects of S. japonica extract against MG infection both in vitro and in vivo, and elucidated its underlying molecular mechanisms. In chicken respiratory epithelial cells, S. japonica extract significantly alleviated MG-induced cellular injury, improved cell viability, reduced apoptosis, and dose-dependently downregulated the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines (TNF-α, IL-1β, IL-6, IFN-γ). Mechanistically, S. japonica suppressed MG-induced activation of the NF-κB signaling pathway by inhibiting the phosphorylation and degradation of IκBα and subsequent phosphorylation of p65. In a chicken MG infection model, S. japonica treatment significantly alleviated clinical symptoms, reduced body weight loss and mortality, elevated serum IgG and IgA levels, and attenuated lung pathological damage. Transcriptome sequencing further confirmed that S. japonica reversed MG-induced gene expression changes, with differentially expressed genes highly enriched in NF-κB, TNF, and cytokine-receptor interaction pathways. Collectively, these findings demonstrate that S. japonica exerts potent therapeutic effects against MG infection, which is associated with suppression of NF-κB-mediated inflammatory responses and enhancement of host humoral immunity. This study provides a scientific basis for the development of S. japonica as a promising alternative agent for the treatment of CRD in poultry.

papers.title: Functionalized Chinese Medicine-Derived Quercetin Carbon Dots for the Treatment of Osteoporosis.
papers.authors: Gan Q, Zhang Y, Wang J, Xue P, Fu Y, Yuan Y
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) compound formulas are widely employed in the clinical management of osteoporosis; however, their principal bioactive constituents and primary molecular targets remain poorly characterized. Consequently, there is an urgent need for systematic functional exploration of TCM-derived chemicals. In this study, we applied a network pharmacology-based approach to screen four canonical TCM compound prescriptions for antiosteoporotic compounds, identifying a total of 20 candidate molecules. Among these, quercetin was selected as a lead compound for the synthesis of biologically active carbon dots (CDs), which were then integrated with mesoporous silica nanoparticles (MSNs) to construct a reactive oxygen species (ROS)-responsive nanocarrier system. In vitro cellular assays demonstrated that both the quercetin-derived CDs and the drug-loaded nanocarriers exhibited excellent cytocompatibility, robust osteogenic-promoting activity, and potent osteoclast-inhibitory effects. Collectively, our findings underscore the utility of network pharmacology in identifying quercetin as a promising TCM-derived lead compound for osteoporosis intervention, and the rational functionalization strategy developed herein provides a valuable paradigm for advancing the therapeutic application of TCM-derived chemicals in bone metabolic disorders.

papers.title: Integrating emerging preservation strategies in cardiac transplantation: From nanotherapeutic frontiers to clinical translation.
papers.authors: Wang H, Wang J, Deng W, Jin F, Lin C
papers.abstract: Hypothermic preservation remains a critical bottleneck in heart transplantation, primarily due to the exacerbation of ischemia-reperfusion injury (IRI) and tightly restricted organ viability windows. Addressing this global clinical crisis requires a departure from traditional monotherapies. This review critically appraises-rather than merely synthesizes-three multidisciplinary advancements: (1) preservation solutions supplemented with nanotherapeutics, with explicit distinction between proof-of-concept, small-animal, and clinically translatable evidence; (2) technological transitions from static cold storage (SCS) to ex vivo heart perfusion (EVHP) and nanowarming-assisted cryopreservation; and (3) bioactive compounds derived from Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM), evaluated through a SWOT framework that acknowledges phytochemical variability and the paucity of clinical transplantation data. We further examine the emerging-but currently nascent and largely speculative---role of artificial intelligence in perfusion decision support. We emphasize that these three domains are not evidentially equivalent: perfusion technology is clinically implemented, pharmacological and nanotherapeutic adjuncts remain predominantly preclinical, and AI applications in cardiac preservation are currently confined to retrospective outcome modelling, with no published closed-loop perfusion control in clinical practice.

papers.title: Non-antibiotic interventions to prevent recurrent urinary tract infections in women: overview of systematic reviews of randomised controlled trials.
papers.journal: The British journal of general practice : the journal of the Royal College of General Practitioners
papers.authors: Santer M, Miller S, Fraser S, Francis N, Lown M, Becque T et al.
papers.abstract:
Recurrent urinary tract infections (rUTIs), that is, ≥2 urinary tract infections (UTIs) in the past 6 months or ≥3 in the past 12 months, are common, have a substantial impact on quality of life, and cause major antibiotic use.
To identify non-antibiotic interventions for prevention of rUTIs that have been assessed in systematic reviews, exploring their effectiveness, acceptability, and adherence.
An overview of systematic reviews of randomised controlled trials (RCTs) on non-pharmaceutical and pharmaceutical (non-antibiotic) interventions for preventing rUTIs in women.
Medline, Embase, CINAHL, Google Scholar, and Cochrane from January 2014 to May 2025 were searched for systematic reviews of RCTs assessing the effectiveness of community-based non-antibiotic interventions for preventing UTI in women aged ≥16 years with rUTIs. Studies in intensive care units, relating to people with indwelling catheters, or comparing different oral antibiotic regimens were excluded. There were no limitations regarding outcome measures or language.
In total, 27 systematic reviews met inclusion criteria evaluating probiotics (n = 9), D-mannose (n = 7), vaginal oestrogen (n = 7), cranberry (n = 6), methenamine hippurate (n = 3), herbal medicine (n = 3), increased fluid intake (n = 2), systemic oestrogen (n = 4), acupuncture (n = 2), and vaccines (n = 2). Eight examined combination strategies. Cranberry and methenamine hippurate use are supported by systematic reviews, as is vaginal oestrogen among postmenopausal women, although questions remain around dose, duration, and treatment adherence. Reviews of probiotics, D-mannose, herbal medicine, acupuncture, and vaccines concluded that stronger evidence is needed. Increased fluid intake benefits women with low intake, but further research is needed on optimal intake. There was little information on treatment adherence or acceptability for many interventions.
For effective interventions, questions remain about promoting adherence (vaginal oestrogen), or optimal preparation (cranberry), or duration (methenamine). For other interventions a stronger evidence base is needed.

papers.title: A Feasible 1H-NMR Quantification Method of Indicator Compounds in Microwave-Processed Reynoutria multiflora Radix and Its Decoction.
papers.authors: Li HZ, Phan HN, Jhang ZH, Chen GF, Yang ML, Wu TS et al.
papers.abstract: Reynoutria multiflora (Thunb.) Moldenke is a commonly used herbal drug in traditional Chinese medicine. Prior literature has indicated that R. multiflora possesses broadband pharmacological activities. According to Taiwan Herbal Pharmacopeia (IV) and previous reports, the dominant components of R. multiflora were 2,3,5,4'-tetrahydroxystilbene-2-O-β-D-glucopyranoside (THSG) (1) and free anthraquinones such as emodin (2), physcion (3), and rhein (4), which played pivotal roles in the pharmacological effects of herbs. However, the standard analytic method with HPLC-UV took much time to prepare samples and calibration curves based on the standard substances. In this study, a rapid quantitative 1H-NMR analytic method has been developed, which can quantify the indicator compounds in R. multiflora samples. The method validation data demonstrated the good accuracy and precision of this qNMR method. The feasible analytical method can monitor the contents of indicator compounds in both raw and processed herbs. In addition, this method could be applied to analyze the indicator compounds in the decoction Qi Bao Mei Ran Dan successfully. These results all supported the proposed method as a useful tool for quality control of R. multiflora herbal materials and decoctions. With further refinement, this method could serve as a reference for future standard methods in pharmacopoeias.

papers.authors: Carlson LE, Deleemans JM, Savard C, Marshall N, Irving ET, Petersson JN et al.
papers.abstract: This review summarizes the definition, diagnosis and prevalence of anxiety and depression symptoms and disorders in people with cancer, followed by an overview of integrative therapies that are guideline-recommended for managing these conditions. Recommended therapies include mindfulness-based interventions, yoga, relaxation, music, reflexology, Taichi/Qigong, acupuncture, lavender aromatherapy and hypnosis. This is followed by a summary of emerging therapies that show preliminary evidence of efficacy, but are not yet included in guideline recommendations, including other forms of aromatherapy, light therapy, biofield therapies, psychedelic-assisted therapy and nature-based interventions. The paper concludes with a summary of common methodological issues and suggestions for future research directions.

papers.title: Machine learning algorithms empower traditional Chinese medicine: Breakthrough approaches from chemical component analysis to pharmacological mechanism research.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.authors: Han Z, Zhao F, Xu H, Zhang Z, Wu J, Zhang Y et al.
papers.abstract: Traditional Chinese medicine studies are constrained by complex chemical components and multi-target biological interactions, making conventional analytical methods inefficient for mechanism exploration. As a data-driven technique, machine learning has been widely adopted to tackle diverse complex challenges in TCM research. Nevertheless, most existing reviews merely summarize individual algorithms or scattered application cases, lacking systematic task-based classification and unified operational standards. Based on literature published from 2022 to 2026, this review systematically classifies machine learning applications in TCM into four core research tasks. A task-oriented framework is constructed to match different algorithms with appropriate TCM research scenarios. This paper further establishes a complete standardized workflow covering algorithm selection, model construction and model evaluation to standardize ML applications in TCM research. This review also summarizes the applications of machine learning in TCM quality control, bioactive compound identification, processing analysis, and mechanism elucidation. Furthermore, major bottlenecks in current ML-based TCM studies are analyzed, and feasible optimization strategies are proposed. This review aims to provide clear and practical guidelines for the standardized application of machine learning in future TCM research.

papers.title: Ratiometric fluorescence determination of phoxim in traditional Chinese medicine matrices using Astragalus residue-derived carbon dots and rhodamine B.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.authors: Wang C, He X, Li X, Dong J, Zhang J, Shao P et al.
papers.abstract: An internally referenced fluorescence method was developed for the determination of phoxim in traditional Chinese medicine matrices. Astragalus residue-derived carbon quantum dots (AR-CQDs) were prepared from Astragalus residue and urea by one-step hydrothermal treatment and combined with Rhodamine B (RhB) to form a dual-emission probe. The AR-CQDs were quasi-spherical, with an average particle size of 4.02 nm, a fluorescence quantum yield of 10.33%, and abundant oxygen- and nitrogen-containing surface groups. Under 320 nm excitation, the AR-CQDs emission at 413 nm served as the response signal, whereas the RhB emission at 580 nm served as the reference signal. Phoxim selectively attenuated the 413 nm emission, and F413/F580 was linearly related to phoxim concentration from 5 to 100 μM (R2 = 0.9952), with a detection limit of 0.106 μM after a 1 min incubation. UV-Vis absorption, fluorescence lifetime, inner-filter-effect correction, zeta-potential, and dynamic light-scattering results suggested that phoxim-induced surface interactions accompanied by aggregation-related effects contributed to the fluorescence attenuation, while the exact microscopic mechanism was not uniquely resolved.In Astragalus, red date, goji berry, and tap-water samples, recoveries were 96.90%-99.60% with RSDs of 1.72%-3.32%, and the results showed acceptable agreement with LC-MS/MS. The method provides a simple ratiometric approach for phoxim screening within the tested matrix and concentration ranges while enabling the analytical valorization of Astragalus residue.

papers.title: Multi-source fusion of NIR and UV spectroscopy with refractometry for pooled prediction of total flavonoids, total polyphenols and solids content in herbal water extracts.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.authors: Gao W, Cheng L, Dong Y, Tao J, Wu Y, Fang C et al.
papers.abstract: Rapid quantification of multiple quality indicators in compositionally distinct herbal formulas calls for predictive approaches that can accommodate pooled samples within a shared modeling framework. To address this limitation, the present study integrates multi-source information from near-infrared (NIR) spectroscopy, ultraviolet (UV) spectroscopy, and refractive index (RI) measurements to develop one pooled model for each of three indicators: total flavonoids, total polyphenols and total solids content in aqueous extracts of six TCM formulas. Six TCM formulas with markedly distinct herbal compositions were selected, and 216 samples were prepared through a gradient extraction protocol. Under a unified SGS + FD pretreatment, three fusion architectures, five feature selection algorithms, and 16 machine learning models were systematically compared. Low-level fusion (LowFusion) performed best for flavonoids and polyphenols before feature selection, whereas mid-level fusion performed slightly better for solids content; the optimal feature selection algorithm was analyte-dependent, and the selected wavelength regions were consistent with plausible electronic-transition and vibrational assignments. Validation using 18 independent samples from new batches of the same six formulas showed strong predictive performance for flavonoids and solids content. The polyphenol model displayed systematic underestimation in the high-concentration range. These results support pooled multi-formula modeling and independent-batch prediction within the investigated formula set, providing a basis for rapid multi-indicator quality assessment without developing a separate model for each formula.

papers.title: Application of a semi-supervised learning framework combining principal component constraint enhancement in near-infrared spectroscopy of Rhizome Coptidis.
papers.journal: Spectrochimica acta. Part A, Molecular and biomolecular spectroscopy
papers.authors: An N, Zhang J, Chen H
papers.abstract: Rhizome Coptidis is a popular traditional Chinese medicinal herb, and analyzing its composition is crucial for evaluating its quality. However, existing analytical methods can produce significantly different results due to various practical factors, so there is an urgent need to develop more suitable analytical methods. Near-infrared spectroscopy (NIR) is widely used in the analysis of traditional Chinese medicine due to its rapid, non-destructive, and pollution-free characteristics. It offers numerous possibilities for the detection of Rhizome Coptidis. However, this technology often encounters challenges such as small sample sizes, limited annotated data, and redundant information. More advanced modeling methods are therefore required to address these issues. Based on this, this paper proposes a fusion framework for the quantitative analysis of Rhizome Coptidis: Spectral Augmented Principal Component Analysis-Semi-Supervised Learning-Convolutional Neural Network-Twin-Kernel Support Vector Regression (SAPCA-SSLCNN-TKSVR). This framework comprises three modules: Spectral Augmented Principal Component Analysis (SAPCA) for data augmentation, Semi-Supervised Learning Convolutional Neural Networks (SSLCNN) for feature extraction, and Twin Kernel Support Vector Regression (TKSVR) for data prediction. The experimental results demonstrate that this method is well-suited to the quantitative analysis of Rhizome Coptidis, particularly in scenarios involving small sample sizes, limited labeled data, and redundant information. It effectively improves modeling performance for high-dimensional, highly linear data and offers a viable approach to the field of near-infrared spectroscopy.

papers.title: Reviewing preclinical evidence for potent anti-colitogenic effects of the "bee glue" propolis.
papers.authors: Quincke SM, Bereswill S, Heimesaat MM
papers.abstract: The incidence and disease burden of inflammatory bowel diseases including ulcerative colitis have risen significantly in recent years, and current treatment remains limited by adverse effects and insufficient long-term efficacy, creating demand for alternative or adjunct treatment options. The "bee glue" propolis, a natural compound with a long history of medicinal use, has attracted growing attention for its anti-oxidant, anti-inflammatory, and immune-modulatory properties. This review summarizes and critically evaluates research into anti-colitogenic effects of propolis and its bioactive molecules in experimental colitis animal models. Our structured literature search revealed 21 preclinical studies showing that application of propolis and derivatives resulted in clinical and histopathological improvement of colitis. Treated animals presented with reduced colonic inflammation, restored intestinal barrier integrity, and a more diverse commensal gut microbiota. Notably, the composition of propolis varied considerably between studies depending on geographical and botanical origins and extraction method of the compound, for instance. In conclusion, propolis and derivatives exert potent anti-colitogenic effects in vivo, and might constitute promising disease-alleviating treatment options in human intestinal inflammation, including ulcerative colitis that should be further unravelled in future clinical trials.

papers.title: Molecular mechanism of total flavonoids of hawthorn leaves in spinal cord injury treatment: A combined network pharmacology and experimental study.
papers.authors: Zhu T, Fu W, Bai Y, Wei R, Huang J, Zeng G
papers.abstract:
Spinal cord injury (SCI) is a devastating neurological disorder characterized by irreversible motor and sensory dysfunction, largely driven by secondary injury mechanisms including oxidative stress, inflammation, and apoptosis. Total flavonoids of hawthorn leaves (TFHL), a traditional Chinese medicine, have demonstrated antioxidant and anti-inflammatory properties; however, their therapeutic effects and mechanisms in SCI remain unclear.
Network pharmacology was employed to identify the active compounds, potential targets, and key signaling pathways of TFHL in SCI through target prediction, protein-protein interaction analysis, and GO and KEGG enrichment analyses. Experimental validation was performed using a rat SCI model, LPS-stimulated BV-2 microglial cells, and RAW264.7 macrophages. Functional recovery was assessed by BBB scoring, while histopathological changes, ultrastructural alterations, inflammatory cytokine expression, and MAPK pathway activation were evaluated using H&E staining, transmission electron microscopy, RT-qPCR, and western blotting.
Network pharmacology analysis identified 15 active compounds and 69 overlapping therapeutic targets, mainly enriched in pathways related to inflammation, oxidative stress, apoptosis, and neuronal survival, including MAPK, PI3K-Akt, TNF, and NF-kB signaling pathways. In vivo, TFHL treatment significantly improved locomotor recovery, alleviated histological damage, preserved mitochondrial structure, and reduced the expression of pro-inflammatory cytokines following SCI. In vitro, TFHL markedly suppressed LPS-induced activation of the MAPK pathway in microglial cells.
TFHL improves functional and histopathological outcomes in SCI models and attenuates inflammatory activation. These effects are consistent with multi-pathway regulation predicted by network pharmacology and are supported, at least in part, by MAPK pathway suppression, warranting further mechanistic and translational studies.

papers.title: Associations of Traditional Chinese Medicine Therapy with Risks of Lower-Limb Amputation, Cardiovascular Mortality and All-Cause Mortality in Patients with Peripheral Arterial Occlusive Disease-A Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.journal: Journal of integrative and complementary medicine
papers.authors: Hu WS, Lin CL
papers.abstract:
This is a retrospective cohort study assessing the association between the use of Traditional Chinese Medicine (TCM) and the risk of lower-limb amputation, cardiovascular (CV) mortality, and all-cause mortality among people with peripheral arterial occlusive disease (PAOD).
The study utilized data from the National Health Insurance Research Database of the Ministry of Health and Welfare of Taiwan. A 1:1 propensity score matching ratio based on gender, age (5-year interval), comorbidities, medications, and year of index date.The risk of outcomes among PAOD patients with and without TCM use was estimated by a Cox proportional hazards model.
The study findings showed that TCM treatment was associated with a significant decreased risk of lower-limb loss (adjusted hazard ratio [aHR] = 0.55, 95% confidence interval [CI] = 0.50-0.61), CV death (aHR = 0.33, 95% CI = 0.31-0.34), and all-cause mortality (aHR = 0.34, 95% CI = 0.34-0.35) among people with PAOD, especially for CV death and all-cause death.
We found that patients with PAOD treated with TCM have a decreased risk of endpoints, especially for CV death and all-cause death.

papers.title: Aloe vera Enhanced Hydroxycamptothecin-Mediated Antitumor Activity in Colorectal Carcinoma Based on the Targeted Regulation of Nucleotide Metabolism.
papers.authors: Wang CY, Li Y, Zhang W, Jiang ZH
papers.abstract:
Colorectal cancer (CRC) remains one of the leading causes of cancer-related mortality worldwide. Combination therapies, which integrate traditional Chinese medicine (TCM) with conventional chemotherapeutic agents, offer a promising new strategy for the management of CRC.
This study aimed to investigate the potential of Aloe vera (L.) Burm.f. (A. vera) as an adjuvant to hydroxycamptothecin (HCPT) for CRC treatment and to explore the underlying mechanisms, specifically focusing on nucleotide metabolism, as perturbations in intracellular nucleotide pools are closely linked to various human pathologies.
The aqueous extract of A. vera adjuvantly ameliorated the progression of colon carcinogenesis was investigated in ApcMin/+ mouse model. For the underlying mechanism studies, cytotoxicity assessment, DNA damage, cell cycle, RNA and DNA synthesis analysis, endogenous nucleotides determination, and Western blot were performed in HCT 116 cells.
Major constituents of A. vera, including aloin A, aloin B, aloesin, aloenin, and aloe-emodin, were quantified and found to meet Chinese Pharmacopoeia standards. A. vera synergistically enhanced the anticancer activity of HCPT. This effect was mediated by exacerbated DNA damage, imbalanced purine/pyrimidine metabolism, and inhibition of the Wnt/β-catenin signaling pathway.
This study provided preliminary evidence that A. vera could be developed as an adjuvant therapy for CRC, contributing to its further clinical application in this field.

papers.title: Ginsenoside Compound K Inhibits Complement C1qA/C3-CR3-Mediated Microglial Synaptic Pruning and Neuronal Pyroptosis.
papers.authors: Zhao X, Liu J, Wang S, Chen N, Zhao J, Zhang Y et al.
papers.abstract:
Ginseng (Panax ginseng C.A. Meyer), a classic traditional Chinese medicine, has long been used for "calming the mind and enhancing intelligence" to combat cognitive decline. Its major metabolite, ginsenoside compound K (CK), exerts neuroprotection, but the molecular mechanisms against Alzheimer's disease (AD) remain unclear.
This study investigated the molecular mechanism by which CK attenuates microglial aberrant synaptic phagocytosis and neuronal pyroptosis via inhibiting the complement C1qA cascade.
APP/PS1 mice were used as AD models and treated with CK (20 or 40 mg/kg/d) or memantine (MH, 3 mg/kg/d) by gavage once daily for 14 weeks. Morris water maze and open field tests were used to assess cognitive function and anxiety-like behavior, respectively. HE, Nissl and Golgi staining detected neuronal damage and synaptic integrity. Immunofluorescence and ELISA measured microglial polarization, activation and synaptic phagocytosis. Molecular docking and dynamics simulations analyzed the CK-C1qA interaction. Western blot, immunofluorescence and ELISA detected complement components (C1qA, C3, CR3) and pyroptosis-related proteins (NF-κB, NLRP3, ASC, caspase-1, GSDMD-N, IL-18). In vitro cellular experiments, including BV2 cell monoculture and BV2-HT22 transwell co-culture systems, were further performed to validate the causal role of C1qA.
CK improved cognitive and anxiety behaviors in APP/PS1 mice, attenuated hippocampal neuronal damage, increased Nissl-positive neurons, restored dendritic complexity and spine density, and upregulated PSD95 and SYP. CK induced microglial M1-like-to-M2-like polarization and reduced Iba1+/CD68+ microglia colocalization with PSD95+ synapses, indicating suppressed synaptic engulfment. CK was predicted to bind to the C1qA globular head domain, reduced C1qA deposition at synapses, inhibited C3, and CR3 expression, suppressed NF-κB phosphorylation, downregulated NLRP3, ASC, cleaved-caspase-1, and GSDMD-N, decreased IL-18 release, and alleviated neuronal pyroptosis. In vitro, CK suppressed C1qA expression in BV2 cells and reduced synaptic C1qA deposition in HT22 cells.
CK ameliorated cognitive and synaptic deficits in APP/PS1 mice by inhibiting the C1qA/C3-CR3 pathway to suppress aberrant microglial synaptic phagocytosis and blocking NF-κB/NLRP3/GSDMD-mediated neuronal pyroptosis. These findings elucidate CK's neuroprotective mechanisms and provide scientific evidence for ginseng's traditional cognitive benefits.

papers.title: Perception and practice of herbal medicine use among people living with HIV in Bushenyi health Centre IV, Western Uganda.
papers.authors: Namitala P, Ngabirano D, Mworozi P, Syed H, Al-Qahtani SA, Mantargi MJS et al.
papers.abstract: BackgroundHerb-drug interactions can affect the outcomes of antiretroviral regimens among people living with HIV. Our study aimed to assess perceptions and practices regarding herbal medicine use among people living with HIV attending Bushenyi Health Center IV in Western Uganda.MethodsWe conducted a cross-sectional, interview-based survey in September 2025 using a pre-validated questionnaire to assess their perceptions and practices of herbal medicine. Participants who were aged more than 18 years, of both genders, on antiretrovial therapy, and who consented to participate were enrolled. Herbal medicine use was defined as the current use of herbal medicine alongside ART. Binary and multiple logistic regression analyses were applied to identify associations with herbal medicine use.ResultsAmong 375 participants, 108 (29%) were concurrently using herbal medicine with ART. Ginger (21%) and garlic (27%) are the commonly consumed herbal products. General health (75%) and boosting immunity (22%) were common reasons for taking herbal medicine. Sixty five (60%) of herbal medicine users did not disclose their use of herbal medicine to their healthcare providers. Low perceived concern (vs. high; AOR = 2.77; 95% CI 1.13-6.82) was positively associated, while low perceived benefit (vs. high; AOR = 0.06; 95% CI 0.02-0.25) was negatively associated with herbal medicine use. Presence of comorbidities, opportunistic infections, experience of side effects of antiretroviral therapy, and non-antiretroviral therapy medication use were significantly associated with herbal medicine use in unadjusted analysis.ConclusionOur study findings underscore the need for open patient-provider communication through co-designed, participatory education models to engage both people living with HIV and healthcare providers in promoting the safe use of herbal medicines alongside antiretroviral therapy. These models address the disclosure gaps and reduce the risk of potential herb-drug interactions.

papers.title: Mild Moxibustion Alleviates Primary Dysmenorrhea in Rats Through TRPV1-Associated Modulation of NF-κB Signaling and Uterine Oxidative Stress.
papers.authors: Bi K, Xiao X, Hou B, Lu R, Zhang R, Zhang Y et al.
papers.abstract:
To investigate the therapeutic effect and analgesic mechanism of mild moxibustion at Shenque (CV8) and Guanyuan (CV4) in a primary dysmenorrhea (PD) rat model, focusing on the involvement of TRPV1-NF-κB signaling and uterine oxidative stress.
Forty female Sprague-Dawley (SD) rats were randomly divided into five groups (n=8): blank group (BG), model group (MG), mild moxibustion group (MMG), antagonist capsazepine group (CPZG), and ibuprofen group (IG). PD models were established through cold stimulation combined with estradiol benzoate and oxytocin injection. The MMG received mild moxibustion at "Shenque" (CV8) and "Guanyuan" (CV4) acupoints. The CPZG was pretreated with capsazepine (CPZ) before moxibustion. The IG received ibuprofen via gavage. After intervention, pain thresholds and writhing scores were measured; uterine pathology was observed via HE staining; ELISA, colorimetric assay, immunohistochemistry (IHC), and Western blotting were used to detect relevant biomarkers.
Mild moxibustion significantly elevated pain thresholds and reduced writhing scores (vs MG, P<0.01). Capsazepine partially reversed these analgesic effects (vs MMG, P<0.01). Mild moxibustion decreased serum IL-1β, TNF-α, and PGF2α while increasing PGE2 (vs MG, P<0.01). Mild moxibustion upregulated TRPV1 expression at acupoints (vs MG, P<0.01), whereas capsazepine suppressed TRPV1 expression (vs MMG, P<0.01). Mild moxibustion downregulated uterine NF-κB P-p65 and COX-2 expression (vs MG, P<0.01), while CPZG upregulated these proteins (vs MMG, P<0.01). Furthermore, mild moxibustion upregulated uterine SOD2 expression (vs MG, P<0.05), decreased MDA content, and increased GSH content and SOD activity (vs MG, P<0.05 or P<0.01).
Mild moxibustion at CV8 and CV4 alleviates PD in rats through mechanisms involving TRPV1 activation, NF-κB pathway modulation, and improvement of uterine oxidative stress. These findings provide a preclinical basis for further investigation.

papers.title: Efficacy and Safety of Integrated Chinese and Western Medicine for Depression With Anxiety and Somatic Symptoms: A Meta-Analysis.
papers.journal: International journal of psychiatry in medicine
papers.authors: Feng Y, Liu W
papers.abstract: ObjectiveSomatic symptoms are often linked with depression and anxiety, making diagnosis difficult and limiting treatment effectiveness. Integrated Traditional Chinese and Western medicine has been studied as a complementary approach; however, its efficacy and safety have not been systematically evaluated. This review and meta-analysis examined the effectiveness and safety of integrated Traditional Chinese and Western medicine in patients diagnosed with depression with or without comorbid anxiety and somatic symptoms.MethodsThis systematic review and meta-analysis followed PRISMA 2020 guidelines. English-language studies published from 2014 to 2026 were searched in PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus. Randomized controlled trials comparing integrated therapy with control interventions were included. The primary outcome was depression severity assessed by HAMD scores. Secondary outcomes included anxiety symptoms, somatic symptoms, and adverse events. A random-effects model was used, and heterogeneity was assessed using the I2 statistic.ResultsEleven studies met review criteria. Integrated therapy significantly reduced depression severity compared with the standard Western medicine control condition (MD = -3.95, 95% CI: -4.71 to -3.19; I2 = 59%). Anxiety symptoms were also significantly reduced (MD = -3.95, 95% CI: -4.65 to -3.26; I2 = 50%). Somatic symptoms, including sleep disturbances and pain-related outcomes, improved but were assessed descriptively because of reporting variability. Adverse events were lower or similar in combined treatment groups, indicating a favorable safety profile. Funnel plot analysis suggested minimal publication bias.ConclusionIntegrated Traditional Chinese and Western medicine was associated with greater improvements in depression and anxiety symptoms than the included control interventions, which comprised Western medicine alone, placebo/sham interventions, or usual care, while showing generally good tolerability. However, given the methodological limitations, heterogeneity of comparator conditions, and low certainty of the available evidence, these findings should be interpreted cautiously.

papers.title: Acupuncture versus reflexology for cancer-related pain in palliative care: a pragmatic study.
papers.journal: Journal of pain and symptom management
papers.authors: Samuels N, Seckbach E, Ben-Arye E
papers.abstract:
Integrative oncology (IO) provides evidence-based therapies addressing symptoms and wellbeing. We compared acupuncture to reflexology for pain and wellbeing among oncology patients.
This comparative effectiveness observational study examined patients undergoing 8 weekly IO treatments with either acupuncture or reflexology, based on patient preference. Symptoms and wellbeing were assessed using the Measure Yourself Concerns and Wellbeing (MYCAW); Edmonton Symptom Assessment Scale (ESAS); and European Organization for Research and Treatment of Cancer Quality of Life Questionnaire (EORTC QLQ-C30).
Of 136 treated patients, 45 (33.1%) chose acupuncture and 91 (66.9%) reflexology. Most were female (111;81.0%), aged 59.7±14.3 years, and Jewish (125; 91.9%). A third had metastatic cancer (45; 34.4%), most undergoing adjuvant treatment (63; 48.1%). Metastatic disease was more prevalent in reflexology-treated patients (OR=2.86; p=0.018; 95%CI=1.20-6.84). Both treatments were associated with within-group improvement on ESAS fatigue, appetite; Total ESAS; and EORTC fatigue, pain and physical, emotional and social function. Only acupuncture was associated with within-group improvement on ESAS pain; and only reflexology on ESAS wellbeing and EORTC Global Health/QoL, nausea/vomiting and insomnia. Reflexology showed a between-group advantage for appetite and cognitive function.
Both acupuncture and reflexology were associated with reduced within-group EORTC pain and ESAS and EORTC fatigue and appetite, physical, emotional and social function; only acupuncture with reduction of ESAS pain; and only reflexology improved wellbeing, somnolence and insomnia, with a between-group advantage for EORTC appetite and cognitive function. Further research is needed to confirm the findings within larger and more diverse patient populations.

papers.title: Potential Mechanisms of N-Methyltyramine in Multitarget Regulation of Mental Disorders via the GPCR-cAMP Pathway.
papers.authors: Zijian W
papers.abstract: N-Methyltyramine (NMT) is a tyramine derivative widely distributed in citrus plants and the traditional Chinese medicine Zhishi. Pharmacological studies have confirmed that NMT directly binds to the dopamine D₂ receptor (DRD2; Ki = 31.3µM), inhibits forskolin-induced cAMP accumulation (EC₅₀ ≈ 4µM, Emax = 89%), and dose-dependently antagonizes quinpirole-mediated β-arrestin2 recruitment, exhibiting G protein-biased agonistic properties. Meanwhile, NMT activates the human trace amine-associated receptor 1 (hTAAR1; EC₅₀ ≈ 2µM) to increase cAMP, possesses α₂-adrenergic receptor antagonistic activity (IC₅₀ = 5.53µM), and exhibits blood-brain barrier permeability (logPe = -5.16cm/s). Based on these multi-target receptor profiles, NMT may participate in the regulation of central monoaminergic neurotransmission via the GPCR-cAMP signaling axis, providing a new multi-target lead compound direction for research on neurological disorders such as Alzheimer's disease, depression, and drug addiction. Notably, evidence for direct activation of β₂-adrenergic receptors by NMT remains insufficient, and its therapeutic effects and downstream signal integration mechanisms require NMT-specific experimental validation.

papers.title: Dahuang Fuzi decoction attenuates renal fibrosis via suppression of the NF-κB pathway.
papers.authors: Liu Y, Niu Z, Guo M, Sun W, Li R
papers.abstract:
Renal fibrosis is a key pathological process in chronic kidney disease with limited treatment options. Dahuang Fuzi Decoction (DFT), a classic traditional Chinese medicine formula, shows therapeutic potential, but its anti-fibrotic mechanism remains unclear.
The anti-fibrotic effect of DFT was assessed in a unilateral ureteral obstruction (UUO) rat model via histopathological examination and renal function tests. The underlying mechanism was investigated using an integrated strategy which included serum pharmacology with drug-containing serum from treated rats, network pharmacology to screen bioactive compounds and predict targets, and in vitro validation in angiotensin II (Ang II)-stimulated NRK-52E cells, with a focused analysis of the nuclear factor κB (NF-κB) signaling pathway.
DFT treatment ameliorated renal injury, reduced collagen deposition, and improved biochemical parameters in UUO rats. DFT-containing serum attenuated Ang II-induced fibrotic responses in cells. Bioinformatics and experimental validation identified the NF-κB pathway as a key target. DFT suppressed p65 nuclear translocation and downstream target gene expression in both UUO kidney tissue and Ang II-stimulated NRK-52E cells, and pharmacological activation of this pathway reversed the protective effects of DFT.
DFT alleviates renal fibrosis, at least in part by inhibiting the NF-κB signaling pathway, as validated in both UUO kidney tissue and Ang II-stimulated tubular epithelial cells, providing a pharmacological basis for its clinical application.

papers.title: Qu's Formula 1 for Anxiety and Depression in PCOS: A Computational Network Pharmacology, Molecular Docking, and Molecular Dynamics Study.
papers.authors: Liu C, Hu W, Zhou J, Wang F, Zhang R, Qu F
papers.abstract: Qu's Formula 1 (QUF1), a patented Chinese herbal medicine, has shown clinical potential in alleviating anxiety and depression in patients with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). This study aimed to investigate potential molecular mechanisms associated with QUF1 using network pharmacology, molecular docking, and molecular dynamics (MD) simulations. Active constituents and potential therapeutic targets of QUF1 were identified using TCMSP and BATMAN-TCM, while PCOS-, anxiety-, and depression-related targets were retrieved from GeneCards, OMIM, and DrugBank. Overlapping targets were used to construct a herb-constituent-target network, followed by Gene Ontology (GO) and Kyoto Encyclopedia of Genes and Genomes (KEGG) enrichment analyses to identify relevant pathways. Molecular docking and 100 ns MD simulations were subsequently used to assess predicted interactions and structural stability between selected constituents and key targets. A total of 76 common targets were identified at the intersection of QUF1 and the disease-related target sets. Protein-protein interaction (PPI) analysis highlighted ALB, TNF, AKT1, IL-6, and ESR1 as key network targets, while KEGG enrichment identified the PI3K-Akt, HIF-1, and FoxO signaling pathways among the relevant pathways. Molecular docking and MD simulations further indicated favorable predicted interactions and generally stable structural behavior for the selected compound-target complexes. These findings support a computational hypothesis that QUF1 may act through a multi-compound, multi-target network associated with inflammatory regulation in PCOS-related anxiety and depression. The results provide a theoretical framework for subsequent experimental and pharmacokinetic validation.

papers.title: Exploring the Molecular Mechanism of Ganoderic Acid B for Insomnia Based on Metabolomics, Network Pharmacology, Molecular Docking, and Experimental Validation.
papers.authors: Wan C, Du Y, Miu J, Chen P, Han Y, Sun S et al.
papers.abstract: Objective: Ganoderma lucidum, a fungus of the genus Ganoderma in the family Polyporaceae, is often used in traditional medicine for the treatment of insomnia and amnesia, etc. Ganoderic acid B, a characteristic lanostane-type triterpenoid isolated from Ganoderma lucidum, has been preliminarily verified to possess mild sedative activity in existing studies. This study aims to explore the potential regulatory mechanism of Ganoderic acid B against PCPA-induced insomnia-like damage via multiple preclinical research strategies, and provide preliminary molecular and experimental clues for subsequent basic mechanistic research of this compound. Methods: Taking Ganoderic acid B as the research object, we established a PCPA-induced mouse insomnia model and evaluated its protective effects on insomnia-associated pathological lesions through behavioral assays, biochemical detection, and cerebral histopathological observation. Subsequently, UHPLC-MS/MS serum metabolomics analysis was performed to screen characteristic biomarkers and pivotal metabolic pathways linked to insomnia pathology. Next, compound and disease target databases were combined to obtain overlapping targets correlated with the alleviation of insomnia lesions by Ganoderic acid B; network pharmacology analyses, including GO and KEGG enrichment, were implemented to screen core hub targets, followed by molecular docking and molecular dynamics simulation to preliminarily verify the binding interaction between Ganoderic acid B and these targets. Finally, an in vitro CORT-triggered HT22 neuronal injury model was adopted for experimental validation, and Western blot assays were conducted on mouse brain tissue to detect the expression of core regulatory proteins. Results: In vivo experiments showed Ganoderic acid B alleviated weight loss and abnormal behaviors, raised serum 5-HT and GABA, and lowered DA and NE in PCPA insomnia model mice. Metabolomics screened six key insomnia-related serum markers, with phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan biosynthesis as the core pathway. CCK-8 assays showed that 4 and 8 μM Ganoderic acid B had no cytotoxicity and relieved CORT-induced neuronal injury, while 16 μM inhibited HT22 cell viability. Network pharmacology identified six core regulatory proteins (EP300, HDAC1, ESR1, IL-6, TNF, NCoR1) mediating Ganoderic acid B's protective effects against insomnia lesions, with Pathways in cancer enriched. Molecular docking verified stable binding between Ganoderic acid B and these targets. Western blot results indicated Ganoderic acid B downregulated NCoR1, EP300, HDAC1, IL-6, and TNF and upregulated ESR1 expression Conclusion: Ganoderic acid B alleviates PCPA-triggered behavioral abnormalities, neurotransmitter disturbance, and hippocampal neuronal injury in mice via multitarget, multipathway synergistic regulation of NCoR1, EP300, ESR1, HDAC1, IL-6, and TNF, and restores the disrupted phenylalanine, tyrosine, and tryptophan biosynthetic network. This work offers preliminary preclinical and molecular evidence to clarify how Ganoderic acid B relieves insomnia-related pathological injuries.
